title: guml.json
description: GUML project configuration. Referenced by `$schema` so editors autocomplete and validate it; the compiler reads the file directly and does not fetch this.

plugins.description: Packages contributing vocabulary, styling, or both. Each entry is a package name resolved through node_modules ("@guml/shadcn") or a directory ("./design-system"). The compiler loads whichever of `guml.registry.json` and `guml.theme.json` it finds inside. Naming a design system's tags and its styling separately is two chances to install one and forget the other, which produces correct tags rendering unstyled — so one entry does both.

registries.description: Explicit paths to registry files, in order. `plugins` covers the common case; this is for a registry not laid out as a package, and for pinning a version.

version.description: Exact version the package must declare. Loading fails on a mismatch: a registry decides which tags a document may use, so a package changing underneath a project changes what its documents mean. Exact rather than a range — semver's 'additive is minor' is the rule this project has evidence against.

theme.description: A builtin name, a path to a theme document, or a plugin that ships one. Omitted means `tailwind`: stock utilities any Tailwind install resolves with no setup. `shadcn` emits design tokens (bg-primary, text-foreground) that resolve only where shadcn's CSS variables are defined.

backend.description: Default target for `guml build`. Seven code generators; the four html-* names are one backend with different styling options.

level.description: `core` compiles markup only — no state, data, actions or js. A host embedding documents it did not write states this once here rather than remembering --core at every call site.
